dedupe_keys.name: gem global earthquake impact database geid past earthquake ground motion and damage data for scenario validation

description: The Global Earthquake Impact Database (GEID) collects earthquake inputs and observed impacts for past events so that seismic risk models can be tested against what happened. It is produced by the GEM Foundation and partners and is organised as a community repository that anyone may extend under contributing guidelines. Coverage: damaging earthquakes worldwide, arranged by country and event, complementing the USGS ShakeMap Atlas and the PAGER loss catalogue with more detailed, often spatially resolved data; release v2023.0.0 is the current tagged version. For each event it holds ready-to-run OpenQuake scenario inputs (rupture solutions, station recordings, ShakeMap-based ground motion fields) and impact records such as building damage counts, casualties and economic losses from reports and the literature. Format and access: a public GitHub repository with CSV, XML and OpenQuake input files, freely downloadable. Licence: Creative Commons BY-NC-SA 4.0, so commercial reuse is excluded. Caveats: impact data come from heterogeneous surveys and reports with different damage scales and completeness, and events are added unevenly by region. Simulation uses: validation and calibration of hazard exposure, fragility and loss models for buildings and infrastructure, and resilience scenarios based on real events. Related records: the OpenQuake Engine (platform-openquake-engine) runs the scenarios, and the GEM Global Exposure Model (data-gem-global-exposure-model) and Global Vulnerability Model (data-gem-global-vulnerability-model) supply the other inputs.
